en: Sutta Nipāta 1.2 Dhaniyasutta “I have cooked my rice and milked my cow;”
(Thus spoke Dhaniya the cowherd:
"On the bank of the Mahī we have our dwelling together;
the hut is thatched and the fire is kindled."
“But if you wish it, O God, rain down.
“I am free from anger and devoid of stubbornness,” [said the Blessed One].
On the riverbank, I have spent a single night’s stay;
the hut is open and the fire is extinguished.
So, O Deva, if you wish, let it rain.
“There are no gnats or mosquitoes here,” said Dhaniya the cowherd,
“the cows graze upon the grass grown thick in the marsh.”
They would endure even the rain that has come;
therefore, O Deva, if you wish, let it rain.
Your raft is bound and well-constructed.
(Thus said the Blessed One:
Having crossed over and reached the further shore, having overcome the flood;
there is no need for a raft.
“But if you wish it, O god, rain down.
“Gopī is obedient to me and not fickle,” [said Dhaniya the cowherd].
She has lived with me for a long time and is dear to me;
I have never heard her say anything evil.
Therefore, O Deva, rain down if you so desire!
“My mind is obedient and liberated,” (said the Blessed One),
“long cultivated and well-tamed.”
"But no evil exists for me;
therefore, O Deva, rain if you so desire.
"I am one who has been hired for my own wages."
(Thus said Dhaniya the cowherd:
"My sons and daughters-in-law are healthy;
I hear no evil concerning them."
“But if you wish it, O God, then rain.
“I am not anyone’s hireling,” [said the Blessed One].
I wander through the entire world having attained my goal;
no need for wages exists for me.
Yet, if you desire it, O God, then rain down.
“There are cows that yield fat,
there are suckling calves,” said Dhaniya the cowherd;
“there are also milch-cows and even those that have recently calved.”
"There is a bull here, the lord of cattle;
if you desire it, O God, then rain.
"There is no steer, there is no suckling calf."
(Thus said the Blessed One:
"There are no female leaders nor even herds;
here there is not even a bull, the lord of cattle."
“But if you wish it, O God, rain down!
“The stakes are firmly driven in and unshakable,” said Dhaniya the cowherd.
The new ropes made of munja grass are well-formed;
even the calves cannot break them,
so if you desire it, O God, pour down rain.
“Like a bull that has broken its bonds,
(said the Blessed One,) like an elephant that has torn apart a rotting creeper;”
"I shall not enter the bed of a womb again,
even if you, O God, desire it; rain down,
filling both the lowlands and the highlands."
A great rain fell at that very moment;
hearing the god raining,
Dhaniya spoke this matter.
“Truly, our gain is not small,
that we have seen the Blessed One;
we go to him for refuge, O Seer of the Eye.”
Be our teacher, O Great Sage.
Both Gopī and I shall be obedient;
let us practice the holy life under the Sugata.
“Having gone beyond birth and death,
may we become those who bring an end to suffering.
“One who has sons rejoices in his sons;”
(Thus spoke Māra the Evil One:
"The cowherd likewise rejoices in his cattle;
for acquisitions are the source of a man's delight."
"For he does not rejoice who is free from acquisitions.
"The one possessed of children grieves because of his children," [said the Blessed One].
The cowherd grieves for his cattle,
and likewise [the householder] grieves for his possessions; for acquisitions are the cause of a man's grief— he who is without acquisitions does not grieve.
The Dhaniya Sutta is the second.
